chosen_line.card: All Streams Flow to the Sea

q1_what_did_you_play: Full aggression into Seapunk, all 3 energy spent on damage plus the free Exhaust attack. All Streams Flow to the Sea first for 9 + 4 from 8 Charge (one point per two Charge) = 13. Then Gorou for 6 at zero cost. Then both Water's Edge for 6 each. Total 31, taking Seapunk from 40 to 9. I eat the telegraphed 11 and drop to 37/70. The point of the line is the threshold: at 9 HP the enemy dies next turn to essentially any hand I can draw — one Water's Edge plus Gorou already does it — so the 11 I take this turn is the last 11 I ever take from this fight. I skipped Tactical Retreat entirely; its random discard could eat All Streams before I cast it, and played after my energy is gone it just churns a hand I'm about to discard anyway. Thoma was priced out: 2 energy for 8 damage and 3 block is worse damage-per-energy than two Water's Edge at 12.
q2_other_line_considered: Yes — the turtle line: both Coral Guard for 10 Block, All Streams for 13, Gorou for 6. That's 19 damage and I take 1 instead of 11, sitting at 47/70 with the enemy at 21. I ran the arithmetic against my line and rejected it. 21 remaining is not a guaranteed one-turn kill from an unknown draw the way 9 is, so the turtle line is likely paying 11 next turn or the turn after and ending up behind on HP anyway, while my line converts this turn's 11 into a closed fight. I also weighed the middle — All Streams, Gorou, one Water's Edge, one Coral Guard: 25 damage, 5 Block, take 6, enemy at 15. It's the worst of both; 15 is still not a reliable one-card kill, so I paid 5 damage of tempo for nothing that changes the number of turns.
q3_what_it_gave_up: 10 HP of face damage, straight up — 48 to 37 instead of 48 to 47. It gives up the two Coral Guard as blank cards this turn, and it gives up all defensive flexibility if the fight goes longer than I think it will: I've spent my whole hand on offence, so a bad draw next turn leaves me at 37 with no Block banked. It also burns Gorou permanently to Exhaust for 6 damage that a spare turn might have used better, and it wastes the 3 Block rider on Thoma, which I never cast. And it accepts the full 11 rather than testing whether Hydro on the enemy does anything — nothing on the page says it does, so I treated the three Hydro applications as flavour, not as damage I'm counting.
q4_different_intent: Yes. If Seapunk had telegraphed a much larger hit — anything from roughly 20 up — the 11-versus-1 gap becomes a survival question rather than a tempo question, and I'd swap the two Water's Edge for the two Coral Guard and take the 19-damage turtle line. A defensive or block-gaining intent would push me harder the other way: no reason to hold anything back, and I'd probably also fire Tactical Retreat looking for another attack since nothing punishes a bad discard. A multi-hit or debuff intent would matter more than the raw number, since 5 Block splits badly across small hits. What would not change my line is a smaller attack — at 8 or below I'm even more comfortable racing.
